stem: A healthcare study measures average patient recovery rate across 4 hospitals, each containing multiple departments. hospital A has 8 observations with mean 70.5 % (within-hospital SD = 7.0). hospital B has 20 observations with mean 81.6 % (within-hospital SD = 7.8). hospital C has 10 observations with mean 81.7 % (within-hospital SD = 8.9). hospital D has 10 observations with mean 87.4 % (within-hospital SD = 4.5). The between-hospital standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 5.0 and 12.6 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true average patient recovery rate for hospital A, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-hospital variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for hospital A: 71.3 % (shrunk from raw 70.5). Range [70.9, 72.6] as between-hospital SD varies from 5.0 to 12.6. Pooled mean: 81.0.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 81.0 % (weighted average of 4 hospital means).
Shrinkage factor for hospital A: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/8). At σ_between=8.4: B = 0.92.
Interval [70.9, 72.6] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (70.5) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (81.0) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
